channel.title: Firearms Industry & FFL Compliance Feed
channel.description: NSSF trade association, FFL regulations, manufacturer updates, and business news.

item.title: Gun Controllers Predicted a Bloodbath. Murders Fell as Gun Rights Expanded.
item.description: Gun control groups predicted more bloodshed as Americans regained firearm freedoms. A new Second Amendment Foundation factsheet documents 85 warnings alongside falling murder numbers, including substantial declines following Bruen and permitless carry.

item.title: Armed DoorDash Driver Stops Attempted Carjacking in Georgia
item.description: A Georgia DoorDash driver walked away after being shoved. When the man returned, threatened to take his car and gun, and attacked him through the driver’s door, he fought back. Deputies call it “a clear case of self-defense.”

item.description: Eight exceptional prize packages valued at more than $20,000 promise to satisfy any enthusiast! WASHINGTON, D.C. — The Project ChildSafe® Safety Sweepstakes is a national fundraising initiative supporting Project ChildSafe, the trusted firearm safety education program dedicated to saving lives and preventing accidents — especially those involvin...

item.title: September Gun Sales Indicator Dips 2.3% as NFA Checks Surge 129%
item.description: September’s firearm-sales indicator slipped 2.3%, but NFA checks more than doubled. With ATF now backing away from federal registration and approval requirements for covered items, the suppressor market could be entering a new phase.

item.title: ATF’s NFA Retreat: Restoring Gun Rights and Pushing for Repeal
item.description: ATF’s nationwide NFA retreat is a major victory. Mark Smith argues wider ownership could strengthen the fight against future suppressor and SBR restrictions.

item.title: Ruger RXM 9mm Pistol – Ruger Meets Magpul
item.description: Ruger and Magpul have come together to create the RXM. This modular pistol promises to be Ruger's most modern pistol.

item.title: PSA 11.5-Inch 5.56 FDE Upper Drops to $299.99 With BCG & Charging Handle
item.description: PSA’s compact 11.5-inch 5.56 FDE upper is now $299.99 with a Carpenter 158 BCG and charging handle included—a $60 savings.

item.title: ATF Stops Enforcing NFA Registration Nationwide for Suppressors, SBRs and More
item.description: Gun-rights litigation has forced a major retreat from the NFA registration scheme. ATF’s October 9 guidance extends non-enforcement nationwide for suppressors, SBRs, SBSs and AOWs, while remaining federal requirements and state restrictions still apply.

item.title: Virginia Students Sue Over Under-21 Gun Purchase Ban and Private-Sale Restrictions
item.description: Two Liberty University students are challenging Virginia laws blocking their private handgun and AR-15 purchases. Boyer v. Katz invokes the Virginia Constitution and follows multiple court victories recognizing the gun rights of adults ages 18–20.

With the balance of power in Washington, D.C., teetering on a pinhead, any dollars […] The post Ev...

item.title: PSA M4A1 Review: Quad Rails, Iron Sights and M4 Nostalgia
item.description: The PSA M4A1 brings back the quad rail, fixed front sight and compact handling of the classic military carbine. We put this semi-auto M4 clone through qualification drills and tested it with iron sights out to 200 yards.

item.title: Speer Gold Dot 9mm 124 Gr +P JHP Battle Pack 250 Rounds — $136.70
item.description: If you have been waiting to stock up on proven 9mm defensive ammo, this deal is worth a look. Ammunition Depot has the Speer Gold Dot 124-grain +P JHP Battle Pack down to $136.70 with code ALand5, giving you 250 rounds of trusted hollow-point ammo in a sealed pack built for long-term storage.

item.title: Smith & Wesson M&P 15-22 Sport Bundle Drops to $399.99 With 3 Magazines
item.description: The popular Smith & Wesson M&P 15-22 Sport is available in a range-ready $399.99 bundle containing three 25-round magazines and a carry case. Its familiar AR-style controls, light recoil and affordable .22 LR chambering make it a practical training and recreational rifle.

item.title: Contra Costa Sheriff Drops Red Dot, Weapon Light and 1911 Carry Bans
item.description: Contra Costa County’s sheriff has agreed to withdraw concealed-carry bans on red dots, weapon-mounted lights and 1911/2011 pistols following a SAF lawsuit. Gun owners should never have needed federal litigation to carry common defensive equipment.

item.title: Maryland Judge Finds Glocks Are Protected Arms, Yet Lets Sales Ban Proceed
item.description: Maryland’s Glock sales ban remains on track for January 1, 2027, after a federal judge recognized the targeted handguns as protected arms but denied preliminary relief. A Connecticut judge blocked a similar restriction, exposing a sharp disagreement over banning lawful pistols because criminals might illegally modify them.

item.title: DOJ Fights Broader NFA Relief After Letting Suppressor Ruling Stand
item.description: DOJ is opposing statewide and nationwide NFA relief after letting the Texas injunction stand. AmmoLand expects ATF guidance within days that could reshape the practical impact for suppressor and SBR owners.

item.title: Everytown’s $10 Million Push Targets Eight House Races and Gun Rights
item.description: Everytown for Gun Safety—the billionaire-backed gun prohibition lobbying group founded years ago by former New York Mayor Michael Bloomberg—is reportedly pumping at least $10 million into eight key congressional races in five states.

item.title: Gun Trace Data Turns Lawful Dealers Into Gun-Control Targets
item.description: A Firearms Research Center analysis exposes how gun-recovery statistics are used to cast suspicion on lawful firearm dealers. The implications reach every FFL: a gun’s later recovery does not establish that the dealer who handled it did anything wrong.

item.title: San Diego Sues Polymaker, Claims 3D-Printer Filament Is a Firearm Precursor Part
item.description: San Diego County, represented in part by Giffords, is suing Polymaker over its ties to gun-printing creators. The complaint argues that firearm-oriented marketing makes certain 3D-printer filaments regulated firearm precursor parts—extending California’s gun-control campaign into raw materials and creator partnerships.

item.title: Everytown Bankrolling Democrats in Midterms Could See Virginia Results Repeated Nationwide
item.description: Everytown is pouring $10 million into electing former Moms Demand Action volunteers to Congress. After Virginia showed what happens when gun owners stay home, the 2026 midterms could determine whether that gun-control agenda spreads nationwide.

item.title: Denver Carry Ban Becomes Latest Fight for Nationwide Gun Rights
item.description: Denver’s open-carry ban and Colorado’s permit restrictions leave otherwise-qualified visitors unable to carry publicly for self-defense. FPC’s lawsuit challenges those barriers in the broader fight to protect gun rights across state lines.

item.title: CZ DUTY: Four Modular 9mm Pistols With Direct-Mount Optics
item.description: CZ’s new DUTY lineup gives gun owners four modular 9mm configurations with compact or full-size grips, optional manual safeties, and direct mounting for several popular red-dot footprints.

item.title: Bodycam Shows Colorado Deputy Stop Charging Black Bear With Handgun
item.description: An Eagle County deputy’s bodycam captured a charging black bear and the rapid handgun response that stopped it. The encounter illustrates the value of firearm proficiency, decisive action, and taking dangerous wildlife seriously.

item.title: CDC Corrects Defensive Gun Use Estimates After Gun-Control Push to Bury Them
item.description: The CDC has corrected its defensive gun use estimates to 500,000–2.5 million annually. The change follows a lobbying campaign by Gun Violence Archive’s Mark Bryant and other gun-control activists that helped get the figures removed in 2022.

item.title: Fact-Denying Anti-Gun Groups Attack DOJ’s Under-21 Handgun Decision
item.description: Teachers Unify condemned DOJ’s conclusion that criminally enforcing the federal dealer handgun ban against law-abiding adults ages 18–20 violates the Second Amendment. Its response overlooks the central issue: these Americans are adults with constitutional rights.

item.title: DOJ Says Gun Owners May Carry in Public National Park Buildings
item.description: DOJ says lawful self-defense carry falls within federal law’s exception for public national park buildings. NPS guidance still tells visitors otherwise.

item.title: NRA Reformers Fusaro and Journey Seek Member Support for 2027 Ballot
item.description: NRA reformers Dennis Fusaro and Phil Journey seek member support for the 2027 board ballot to continue rebuilding accountability and advancing gun rights.

item.title: Everytown Pushes AI Gun Restrictions That Could Censor Lawful Firearms Information
item.description: Everytown wants a say in what AI chatbots tell gun owners. Its latest report calls for firearms information restrictions that extend beyond preventing suicide and criminal violence, raising concerns about access to information on lawful gun ownership.

item.title: Russia Plague Scare After Lab Worker’s Death Highlights Need for Preparedness
item.description: A worker’s unexplained death at Russia’s Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute has sparked international concern, with nearly 200 contacts reportedly under medical observation. Plague remains unconfirmed, but the incident is a reminder to prepare before an emergency, including respiratory protection.

item.title: Oklahoma Guardsman Faces D.C. Gun Felony as Congress Stalls on Carry Reciprocity
item.description: Ordered to Washington for a National Guard deployment, Jakob Noonan now faces a felony charge for carrying a handgun without a D.C. license. His case shows the consequences of a carry-rights patchwork Congress has repeatedly promised to fix.
